critique: The near-black background, yellow-green emissive color, and soft local halos are visually on target. At t4 the field is sparse and has a convincing mix of dimmer and brighter fireflies, with no rain- or snow-like directionality. However, the population remains temporally inconsistent: t1 contains only two visible lights and feels nearly empty, while t4 has roughly ten. This reads more as particles accumulating after emission begins than a continuously inhabited firefly field. The two sampled stills also do not yet make the intended slow wandering motion clearly legible.

suggestions.why: Raise the emission rate so the early sample contains a small but readable firefly population instead of only two isolated lights.
Shorten lifetime while raising emission so the t4 population stays sparse and reaches a stable count sooner, reducing the visible accumulation between t1 and t4.
